day_shape: 74 items: Pezeshkian addresses UNGA calling US and Israel terrorists, OFAC publishes Iran GLs Y and Z, CENTCOM says 115 vessels redirected under Hormuz blockade, Canada sanctions 10 Iranian targets, Hamas finance chief killed in Khan Younis strike.

threads.label: Pezeshkian at UN General Assembly
threads.summary: Iranian President Pezeshkian addressed the UNGA calling the US and Israel 'terrorists' and holding sidelines meetings with the leaders of Iraq, Norway and Switzerland. Regime channels amplified the speech and quoted Reuters, Washington Post and Politico coverage; Syrian President al-Sharaa also addressed the Assembly.

threads.label: US-Iran indirect diplomacy in New York
threads.summary: Iran's foreign ministry said it conveyed conditions for ending hostilities via Qatari mediators, while Rubio reaffirmed US defence commitments to Saudi Arabia and referenced indirect contacts with Tehran. Iran International reported divisions in Tehran over negotiating authority, and INSS's Beni Sabti told the Jerusalem Post the reported Witkoff-Kushner track was a 'half-truth'.

threads.label: Sanctions, OFAC licences and aviation squeeze
threads.summary: OFAC published Iran-related General Licenses Y and Z, Canada sanctioned five Iranian individuals and five entities, and the UAE central bank imposed measures on Bank Melli branches. Iran International reported Iranian carriers continued international flights past the US deadline, with Tehran threatening to disrupt regional airports that comply.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz maritime pressure
threads.summary: CENTCOM said its forces have redirected 115 commercial vessels enforcing what it called a 'steel wall blockade', with a further statement from Adm. Brad Cooper. The Jerusalem Post reported two casualties after a cargo vessel was struck in the Strait, and Iran International reported oil pollution spreading along the Hormozgan coast.

threads.label: Gaza and West Bank operations
threads.summary: The IDF reported killing a car-ramming attacker at a Binyamin Brigade checkpoint after a reservist was severely wounded, and located a 600-metre tunnel crossing the Yellow Line in central Gaza. Netanyahu and Katz announced the killing of Hamas finance chief Mohammed Abu Alwan in a Khan Younis strike, and a $2.45bn six-month Gaza reconstruction plan was reported.

threads.label: Sistan-Baluchestan clash and mobilisation
threads.summary: Defa Press and IRIB said IRGC Brigadier General Hossein Zarifi, commander of the Shahid Sajjad Saravan operational headquarters, was killed in counter-terrorism operations, with the Sistan-Baluchestan governor's office reporting several militants killed in Saravan. Basij chief Taib claimed over 30 million volunteers and announced the opening of the first specialised volunteer training base in Tehran's Imam Hossein Square.

threads.label: Domestic Iran repression and hardship
threads.summary: Iran International reported the execution of IT expert Hossein Pedaran after months of solitary confinement and a forced confession, and a hacked Los Angeles freeway sign directing drivers to a site threatening Islamic Republic opponents. Iran's Education Ministry confirmed thousands of primary-age children cannot attend school due to financial hardship, and a Swiss court rejected the asylum bid of Iranian convert Behnam Vali Heydarian.

events.title_en: 'A shameful spectacle'; Macron's view on Trump's peace plan. French President Emmanuel Macron, in his speech to the UN General Assembly, rejected US claims about Gaza and emphasised that 'not even a single humanitarian corridor in this region has been reopened.' This French official strongly criticised Trump's claims about establishing peace in Gaza and said: 'The world is witnessing a spectacle that should be a source of shame for everyone.' Macron made these remarks at a time when, before him, Donald Trump, in his speech to the UN, referred to the Gaza peace plan as 'a diplomatic victory'.
